question_text: Receivables net = $2285M. What does net mean here?
option_b: After subtracting the allowance for uncollectible accounts
explanation: Net always means something was subtracted. For receivables: Gross A/R minus the Allowance for Uncollectible Accounts = Net Realizable Value — the amount expected to actually be collected.

question_text: Deferred Membership Fees ($2337M) is a LIABILITY. Why?
option_b: Costco received cash but has NOT yet earned the revenue (time has not passed)
option_c: These are fees that were never paid
option_d: It represents discounts owed to members
explanation: Revenue recognition: Costco cannot record membership revenue until time passes. When a member pays upfront Costco records a liability (deferred revenue) because it still owes the customer access to the warehouse for the remaining period.

question_text: Accounts Payable ($17483M) is greater than Merchandise Inventories ($16651M). What does this mean?
option_a: Costco has more debt than assets
option_b: Costco has not paid for any of its inventory — suppliers are financing it
explanation: Costco sells inventory to customers BEFORE paying suppliers for it. They owe suppliers more than the value of goods on shelves — meaning suppliers effectively finance all of Costco inventory. This is a key competitive advantage.

question_text: Accrued Member Rewards ($2150M) appears under Liabilities. Who is this owed to?
option_c: Executive members who earned 2% cashback rewards not yet paid out
explanation: Executive members earn 2% back on purchases. This accumulates as a liability because Costco has promised this money to customers but has not paid it out yet. It is owed to members not employees or suppliers.

question_text: Property Plant & Equipment is reported net. Net of what?
explanation: PPE is reported at Historical Cost MINUS Accumulated Depreciation. This is called the book value or carrying value. It represents the remaining undepreciated cost — not the current market value.

question_text: Costco Net Income ($6292M) is higher than Membership Fee Revenue ($4580M). What changed vs pre-2019 strategy?
option_b: Costco started breaking even on all sales keeping only membership fees
option_c: Post-2019: Costco now earns a small margin on merchandise sales in addition to membership fees
explanation: Pre-2019 Costco intentionally broke even on all sales — net income approximated membership fees. Post-2019 they began generating a small margin on merchandise. Net income now exceeds membership revenue because they keep a portion of every sale on top of membership fees.
